newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki falls after Wall Street falters.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki falls after Wall Street falters.

text.p: Shares closed broadly lower on Wednesday after a choppy, moderately traded session, as overnight losses on Wall Street and profit-taking reversed recent index gains, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 1.21 percent to 2,369.79. Volume was fair at 412 million, with more than one third of it in telecommunications share Nokia.
Nokia closed down 9.40 markka at 253.00, off 3.6 percent, after recovering from an intrasession low of 251.00 markka.
Brokers said investors were squaring positions ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S. on Thursday -- some of them apparently for speculative reasons.
"Some of them probably think they can buy their shares back for even less when New York is closed," one broker said.
Profit-taking also hit finance sector shares after a week of steady gains, with banking share Merita falling 0.40 markka to 14.40.
But brokers said Merita was still likely to test its 15.00 markka resistance in the near-term.
Forestries were soft, despite a report from the forest industry federation saying that an upturn lies ahead.
UPM-Kymmene fell 0.50 markka to 89.50, and Enso shed 0.20 to close at 34.80 markka.
"The outlook for forestries remains uncertain," one broker said. "The forestry federation's report did not clarify the picture."
Other brokers attributed the weakness in forestries to the general softness at home and to lower U.S. paper shares.

Shipping group Finnlines climbed 2.80 markka in brisk trade to 112.00. Volume rose above 50 million markka, or 10 percent of total bourse turnover. Brokers said demand came from foreign investors but otherwise could not explain the surge.
Shares in plastic pipes, white goods and furniture maker Asko made strong gains in heavy trading sparked by the company's recently announced streamlining plans, brokers said.
